reason: Both responses satisfy every hard requirement (correct headings/order, snapshot-before-risk gating, no restart/failover before snapshot, explicit abort conditions), but Response A layers abort/rollback conditions at each phase (detection false-alarm, snapshot-stall, and post-mitigation non-improvement) and adds more concrete operational diagnostics (e.g., corroborating alerts via two independent sources, distinguishing I/O wait vs. log-flush backpressure vs. autovacuum as latency causes, verifying replica lag before considering failover), making it a more robust and actionable runbook than Response B's slightly thinner single abort condition.
